records.region: Southwestern Buenos Aires Province, Argentina; Sierra de la Ventana–Saldungaray, Paso de las Piedras, Paso Mayor and Monte Hermoso–Sauce Grande coastal corridor.
records.material_pending_reason: The named river, distinct headward component, reservoir, lake and lower approach have readable primary correspondence, but the final selected coastal connection is not demonstrated. This is one source-material-pending case, not a completed representative assignment or completed naming-scope hold.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río Sauce Grande is a bounded receiving-system candidate. The selected Nacimiento/Destierro Primero opening, Paso de las Piedras reservoir, middle river, Laguna Sauce Grande and eastward lower approach are supported. The final selected southward dune crossing lies west of the outlet depicted by the successful maps and remains unestablished.
records.completion_scope: The unchanged one-fragment,36-part selection was compared against a successfully acquired historical topographic original and the independently authored doctoral study's original maps, including the headward opening, upper joins, reservoir passage, middle river, lagoon, lower outflow and the selected terminal. A substantial final coastal connection remains unestablished. The supported Sauce Grande candidate is retained with one primary material-pending status, no accepted scalar and no application.
records.supported_name_scope: The mapped Sauce Grande river corridor through the intermontane valley, Paso de las Piedras reservoir, downstream plain and Laguna Sauce Grande outlet approach. The headward Nacimiento/Destierro Primero component and the two standing-water bodies retain their distinct identities.

component_scope_limits: Sauce Grande is a bounded receiving-system candidate, not a uniform scalar for the headward stream, reservoir, lagoon and unresolved terminal.
The opening is mapped as Nacimiento or Destierro Primero; its precise naming transition into Sauce Grande is not fixed.
Basin membership or a nearby named river mouth does not establish the selected dune crossing.
Historic cartography and the thesis do not establish current dam operations, current lake/river flow permanence or a formal current name registry.

records.region: Ancash–Lima, Peru; upper Pativilca valley through Chiquián, Cahua and the Pacific outlet north of Barranca.
records.candidate_name_role: Provisional representative receiving-river/system candidate supported for the mapped main valley and Pacific outlet. The selected initial headward branch connection is not fully established, so this is not a completed representative-system assignment.
records.material_pending_reason: The selected first headward branch and its receiving join remain unestablished among the mapped northern feeders; downstream main-valley and Pacific-mouth correspondence does not resolve that opening.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Río Pativilca is a provisional candidate for this selection. The 1985 INGEMMET map and study support the main valley, major tributary joins and Pacific outlet north of Barranca, but do not securely establish the selected first headward branch. The record remains material-pending, with accepted, scalar and Korean names null and product application false.
records.completion_scope: One primary material-pending record. The source-map review covered the full extent visually, including all major downstream joins and the actual coast, but the first selected headward branch connection remains unestablished. This is neither completed representative identity nor completed name-scope hold. The cancelled source acquisition is factual access detail, not a second primary pending count.

records.region: Southwestern Greenland, inland ice and the historical inner Sermilik ice-front/fjord setting east of Paamiut.
records.candidate_name_role: No representative natural-river identity established; the source-labelled Sermilik fjord setting is context only.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The whole selected inland-ice, ice/bedrock-margin and historical inner Sermilik terminal setting is visible in the two original maps, but they do not establish one named continuous natural river along the modeled line.
records.geographic_disambiguation: FID 8914 opens inland in the southwestern Greenland ice sheet and runs southward before its lower westward turn across the ice/bedrock margin. The 1995 national original covers the opening and northern corridor beyond the regional sheet boundary; the 2007 Sheet 1 original overlaps the southern ice corridor, exposes the lower turn, and continues through the FID 8914–8915 junction and the entire short western FID 8915 to the historical inner Sermilik ice-front/fjord setting. Ice, exposed bedrock, coastal water and cartographic contour/geological symbols are distinguished. No source maps this modeled sequence as one continuous named natural river.
records.completion_scope: Both fragments and all 34 stored parts were compared with the newly acquired original geographic graticules, mapped terrain and coastal setting. National and regional coverage overlap around the 62°30′N regional boundary. The lower loop/turn, fragment junction and actual final selected endpoint are covered. No substantial unviewed interval remains at ordinary terrain/corridor scale; exact banks, name-change vertices, present-day ice-front position and hydraulic continuity are outside this finding.

component_scope_limits: Sermilik is retained solely as the directly read geographic context label of the fjord setting, not as the selected river name.
No glacier or other local name is inferred for an unlabelled selected section.
The stored sea-terminal class and continuous model parts do not independently prove a present-day natural river or ordinary river mouth.
The maps are historical thematic cartography. A current web acquisition is not a contemporary drainage or glacier-front survey.
A null candidate means that this research did not establish the name; it does not assert that no local or official name exists.

publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
